Synthetic demonstration alert, not tied to a detection. Ingestion deliberately delayed ~45s after event_time_utc to exercise event-time vs ingestion-time handling.

scenario_events.description: A debris object first appears in the study area (drifts into it) at t=600s rather than being present at mission start.
Platform passes close to a static object multiple consecutive frames in a row, producing several detections tied to one track.
A designated in-range object is deliberately withheld from detection output for this window (simulated occlusion), even though it remains within nominal sensor range.
Platform GPS location_uncertainty_m is inflated and a single position discontinuity is injected to emulate a GPS noise event.
One alert's ingestion_time_utc is set ~45s after its event_time_utc to demonstrate event-time vs ingestion-time handling. Instantaneous scenario (start==end).

Telemetry and imagery sampling is suspended for this window: sequence numbers skip over it entirely. This is an intentional gap, not missing/corrupt data — validate.py checks for exactly this gap and expects it.
